title: Reserve allocator and autoscale safeguards: predictable reserved capacity with tenant surge isolation
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD defines a reserve allocator and autoscale safeguard layer for Dedicated capacity aimed at providing predictable reserved throughput for tenants while protecting the cluster from noisy neighbor surges. The feature introduces per-tenant reservoirs, a configurable headroom buffer, and a graceful preemption/eviction window. It also specifies operator controls and observability to ensure safe rollouts and clear incident remediation paths.
problem_statement: Customers with Dedicated (reserved) capacity require strong guarantees that committed tokens/throughput remain available during normal operations while still allowing bounded, auditable transient burst behavior. Current behavior either over-allocates headroom (wasting capacity) or allows bursts to degrade other tenants' SLOs without clear eviction or fallback policies.
background: We already support reserved pools and some burst policies, but feedback from enterprise customers and SRE indicates the need for: 1) a deterministic allocator that reduces fragmentation across zones, 2) clear tenant-level isolation thresholds, and 3) autoscale safeguards that prevent runaway preemption during cluster-wide scale events. This PRD proposes an allocator + safeguard pattern that balances predictability and efficient utilization.
goals: 1) Guarantee reserved throughput for committed tenants within defined SLO windows. 2) Provide bounded soft-bursting with measurable grace periods that are reversible. 3) Expose operator controls to tune headroom, preemption thresholds, and eviction policies. 4) Deliver telemetry and acceptance tests for correctness and regression detection.
non_goals: 1) This PRD does not replace the full scheduler rewrite. 2) It does not introduce per-request billing changes. 3) It will not modify on-prem networking or KMS integrations.
user_stories: As a platform customer I want my reserved capacity to sustain baseline traffic even when other tenants spike, so my production features keep latency SLOs.
As an SRE I want an autoscale safeguard that prevents mass preemption from causing cascading evictions across tenants during a rapid cluster scale-down.
As an operator I want to set and adjust a cluster headroom parameter and observe its utilization so I can tune utilization vs safety trade-offs.
As a tenant admin I want to see a clear audit trail when my burst credits are consumed and when preemption occurs, so I can justify capacity purchases to stakeholders.
requirements: R1: Introduce per-tenant reservoir objects that record committed units, ephemeral headroom, and burst credits.
R2: Allocator must allocate capacity by reservoir in a way that minimizes cross-zone fragmentation and respects tenant affinity tags.
R3: Provide a cluster-wide headroom parameter (percentage of cluster reserved for safe burst) and a tenant-level cap on burst consumption.
R4: Implement a graceful preemption window: when capacity is constrained, mark surplus ephemeral allocations as preemptible and wait N seconds before evicting to allow rollback or fallback routes.
R5: Autoscale safeguards: the autoscaler must not trigger preemptions that would drop more than M tenant baseline slots in a single minute (operator-configurable).

R6: Audit logging for reservoir events: allocation, burst debit, preemption mark, eviction executed, and rollback. Logs must include tenant, pool, zone, timestamp, reason, and correlating request IDs.
R7: Expose operator APIs and Console controls to adjust headroom, per-tenant caps, and emergency reclaim policies (with change history).
R8: Provide end-to-end regression tests and chaos scenarios that validate SLO preservation for reserved tenants under spike conditions.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: In test harness, a tenant with committed 100 units should retain >=95% of baseline throughput under a synthetic cross-tenant spike for a 10-minute window when headroom configured to 10%.
AC2: Autoscaler changes that would cause >20% of committed baseline slots across tenants to become preemptible in <2 minutes are rejected by safeguard logic (configurable thresholds).
AC3: Audit logs for a simulated eviction sequence contain required fields and are queryable from Console within 30s of event emission.
AC4: Console UI displays per-tenant reservoir state (committed, used, headroom, burst_credits) with live update frequency <=15s.
AC5: Can perform controlled rollback of a headroom parameter change within 5 minutes with no more than 1% incident-level customer-impact deviation compared to baseline.
AC6: Release tests include chaos scenario where zones are partially degraded and system maintains reserved tenant baseline throughput within SLA for 90% of tenants.
AC7: Documentation and operator runbook published and linked from Console help menu prior to GA rollout.
AC8: Security review signoff (if later required) must be trackable; for initial launch security_review_required set to false but process must be documented.
api_contract: GET /api/dedicated/v1/reservoirs/{reservoir_id} - reservoir state (committed, used, headroom, credits, zone_allocations)
Events: reservoir.allocated, reservoir.burst_consumed, reservoir.preempt_marked, reservoir.evicted (emitted to event bus)
console_ui_changes: New 'Reservoirs' tab under Dedicated -> Capacity showing per-tenant cards and aggregated charts.
Operator panel to adjust cluster headroom and emergency reclaim with audit trail and soft-confirm modal.
Time-series line charts for reserved baseline utilization, burst consumption, and preemptible counts with selectable windows.
Drill-down view showing last 24h of reservoir events and links to correlated logs/PRs/incidents.
telemetry_and_metrics: logs: structured JSON events for audit entries available in Logstore with index on tenant_id and reservoir_id
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: enable allocator in 5% of clusters (non-production tenants) for 2 weeks and run synthetic spike tests. 2) Gradual ramp: enable for 25% of customer clusters with operator monitoring for 1 week. 3) Soft GA: opt-in release for dedicated customers with documentation and runbook. 4) GA: default enable for new Dedicated contracts and migration path for existing customers. Each stage requires signoff from SRE, Product, and Legal (if contract wording changes).
dependencies: ENG-232100: allocator core implementation and zone-aware placement
ENG-238122: events bus schema changes for reservoir events
DES-44100: Console UX for Reservoirs tab
SEC-1002 (optional): security audit for audit-log retention policy
migration_steps: 1. Create reservoir records for all committed tenants using billing-backed committed_units snapshot.
2. Simulate allocations in staging with mirrored traffic and reconcile differences under a 'dry-run' allocator mode.
3. Schedule a low-risk migration window for tenants with complex multi-zone footprints; provide opt-out toggle for customers during migration.
4. After migration, monitor headroom and utilization for 72h before moving to soft GA.
5. Provide rollback instructions to revert reservoir assignment and headroom adjustments within the operator Console.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly conservative headroom reduces utilization and increases customer costs. Mitigation: provide default conservative value + operator tuning guide and auto-suggest based on historical utilization.
Risk: Preemption cascade inadvertently evicts high-priority tenants. Mitigation: implement max_preemptible_rate and preemption window; require canary validation and operator alerting.
Risk: Fragmentation across zones reduces scheduler efficiency. Mitigation: allocator uses zone-aware packing heuristics and periodically compacts reservoirs during low traffic windows.
Risk: Ambiguous audit logs make incident forensics slow. Mitigation: enforce structured event schema and expose a Console query template for common investigations.
open_questions: Q1: Default values for cluster headroom and preemption window? Proposed 10% headroom, 60s preemption window for initial canary.
Q2: How should burst credits be priced/charged for committed customers? Discussion required with Pricing team.
Q3: Should we expose per-tenant emergency reclaim toggle to tenant admins or only operators? Security and abuse considerations.
Q4: Do we need gRPC equivalents for API endpoints above or is REST sufficient for GA?
